title: Odoo Procurement Automation
summary: Bringing RFQs, purchase orders, payment notices, and pickup scheduling from Odoo into suppliers’ WhatsApp conversations.
context: Monotaro Indonesia connects business buyers with many suppliers. For products without known supplier stock, procurement needs to check availability before proceeding. As buyer demand increased, a small procurement team had more supplier follow-ups to handle. RFQs already went out by email, but many suppliers were more responsive on WhatsApp. The project brings those procurement actions into the channel suppliers actually use.
features: Send RFQ inquiries from an Odoo action.
Deliver purchase orders, payment documents, and pickup notices.
Reach up to five alternative suppliers per SKU.
flowNote: The queue/function stage represents intermediate processing between the Python entry function and the GCP sending instance. Individual automation flows are shown with their descriptions below.

workflows.title: RFQ inquiry & reply review
workflows.body: A procurement team member sends an RFQ inquiry with a button in Odoo. A batch process analyzes supplier replies using AI and updates the purchase order’s RFQ WA Status field, including statuses for problems such as a price mismatch. Clean results can proceed to automatic RFQ confirmation and PO sending.
workflows.detail: Incoming messages are collected by a GCP instance, stored in Cloud SQL, and flow into BigQuery. Functions and a task queue also deliver messages to the Chatwoot conversation interface.

workflows.title: Purchase-order delivery
workflows.body: Confirming an RFQ triggers delivery of the PO document to the supplier through WhatsApp.

workflows.title: Payment-document delivery
workflows.body: Procurement emails are ingested into BigQuery, and bank payment notifications are converted into PDFs. The document is passed to Odoo for delivery through WhatsApp, reducing manual payment notifications.

workflows.title: Pickup scheduling
workflows.body: Procurement sets the pickup field in Odoo, which triggers the supplier message with the pickup schedule.

workflows.title: Alternative supplier outreach
workflows.body: When the primary supplier has no stock, the vendor-alternative team can trigger outreach to up to five alternative suppliers per SKU with a button, replacing separate manual messages to each vendor.

decisions.title: Meet suppliers in their existing channel
decisions.body: Email RFQs were already part of the process, but many went unanswered. WhatsApp group conversations fit how these suppliers actually communicated, so the integration was shaped around that workflow.

decisions.title: Make the message easier to answer
decisions.body: The RFQ templates were refined with clearer wording and an easier reply format, helping suppliers respond to the inquiry in a useful way.

title: ChatDesk
focus: Customer conversations & template outreach inside Zendesk
summary: A Zendesk sidebar app for customer WhatsApp conversations, ticket-to-template field mapping, and outreach logging.
context: Customer service already used Zendesk for tickets, but WhatsApp outreach meant switching tabs and copying ticket values into message templates. ChatDesk provides a custom Zendesk sidebar interface connected to Chatwoot, with ticket fields mapped into the app and WhatsApp templates. An earlier usage check put total message volume at roughly 50–100 messages per day.
features: Open the customer’s conversation from the ticket’s phone number.
Map Zendesk fields to app inputs and WhatsApp template parameters.
Record each template send in the Zendesk ticket.

workflows.title: Open the right customer conversation
workflows.body: The customer phone number on the Zendesk ticket is mapped into ChatDesk’s custom sidebar interface. The interface connects to Chatwoot so agents can review the customer’s messages and send a WhatsApp message while staying inside Zendesk.

workflows.title: Prepare WhatsApp templates from ticket fields
workflows.body: Zendesk fields map to app inputs and WhatsApp template parameters, reducing repeated copying between tools. The ChatDesk backend calls Chatwoot, which sends the message through the Meta WhatsApp API.

workflows.title: Keep template outreach in the ticket record
workflows.body: Each template message send is recorded in its Zendesk ticket, keeping a record of the outreach alongside the support work.

title: Meilisearch Integration
summary: Direct product suggestions in the search bar, backed by daily index rebuilds and product-focused relevance tuning.
context: The previous search bar suggested search terms: typing “Paper” could suggest searching for “Paper” again. With Meilisearch, the dropdown shows matching paper products directly. Backend indexing and relevance configuration support the product suggestions presented in the search bar.
features: Surface matching products directly in the search-bar dropdown.
Rebuild the product index from BigQuery data every day.
Configure relevance using product attributes, activity counts, and synonyms.
miniNote: Product suggestions in the search bar
workflowTitle: From a query to a product.
metricsNote: CTR refers to clicks on product suggestions in the search bar.

workflows.title: Show matching products in the search bar
workflows.body: Typing “Paper” brings up matching paper products in the search-bar dropdown. Indexing, result-field selection, and ranking configuration provide the backend support for those product suggestions.

workflows.title: Rebuild the catalog index every day
workflows.body: A Cloud Run job queries product data stored in BigQuery and builds a fresh Meilisearch index each day. The catalog contains around six million SKUs. The active index is switched only after the replacement is built successfully; the old index is then removed. Products absent from the new snapshot are excluded.
workflows.detail: A failed rebuild triggers an automatic retry. If that also fails, the existing index remains active and rebuilding is attempted again another day.

workflows.title: Tune relevance around product attributes
workflows.body: Model, brand, and product name are the key product fields for relevance. Search counts and purchase counts are included as ranking inputs, with synonyms configured to connect related search terms. The configuration also determines which product fields are returned for the suggestions.

outcome: Product suggestions in the search bar recorded a 5% click-through rate.

title: Stock Count Management
focus: Stock-count sessions, count sheets & recount cycles
summary: An Oracle APEX application for stock-count sessions, printable QR-linked sheets, and recount cycles, with Odoo file import and export.
context: SCM is designed for Finance and Accounting teams auditing warehouse stock. It organizes quarterly and annual stock-count sessions, including annual counts split into parts. Location-based count sheets, review cycles, and Odoo file exchange support the count from preparation to its final export. The application has not yet entered operational use.
features: Organize stock-count sessions and preserve their history.
Generate printable, QR-linked count sheets by location.
Manage recount cycles and exchange stock files with Odoo.

workflows.title: Organize count sessions and their history
workflows.body: Quarterly and annual counts are organized as separate sessions, with annual counts also divided into parts. Past sessions are documented and can be restored when needed.

workflows.title: Create a session from an Odoo stock file
workflows.body: An Odoo stock_quant file can be uploaded into SCM to create a new stock-count session.

workflows.title: Generate count sheets by location
workflows.body: Stock lines are divided into location-based count sheets, called papers in the application. Each paper can be generated as a printable PDF for the count.

workflows.title: Manage line-level recount cycles
workflows.body: Each paper has a count cycle. Rejected lines generate a new paper and a new cycle, allowing items to be counted again as needed.
workflows.detail: A supervisor can force-accept a discrepant line when needed.

workflows.title: Open the matching sheet from its QR code
workflows.body: Each PDF includes a QR code containing the paper’s ID. Scanning it inside SCM opens that count sheet directly.

workflows.title: Export count results back to Odoo
workflows.body: The stock-count result can be exported as a CSV file for import back into Odoo.
